streetview.pano_ids_note: the three Google panoramas a sight-line test over the LiDAR finds most open to the building (2024-08, 31-33 m, on Eden Crescent off its north-east end, the street end: 64-66%, 28% of its roof clear of buildings and trees). 34 panoramas lie within 80 m; the others see 18% or less.
streetview.camera_fixes_note: the three panoramas of 2024-08 record their cameras about 1 m to the right of where the LiDAR puts the street end, as seen from the street (round 1, 2026-10-27, parts/common.js): v8ia's camera fitted to its wide view's own edges (the end's two side edges at rows 50 and 150, columns 360 and 1490, on the LiDAR's edges of the end at z -9.6 and +10.9; the two piers' feet, rows 772-780, on the street at -0.75 m) is 0.32 m nearer and 1.06 m to the left (residuals 0.08 m or less); the same fit to the street end's drawn openings (bays, window bands, vehicle way) moves mdk1's 0.87 m and MH15's 1.39 m to the left (rms 10 and 8 px over 12 and 9 points). All three the same way, from one drive: an offset between Street View's positions and the LiDAR, not a model's error. Their views are cut from the panoramas as before; only the camera they are drawn from moves

light.note: the viewer's light for this building (pipeline/viewer/main.js; the address still wins). The three panoramas (2024-08) show the street end, which faces north-east (bearing 44.5 deg), with no shadow cast on it by its piers, its top storey or its canopy, and sunlit patches on the street in front: the end is in open shade, so the sun was behind it, past bearing 314.5 deg, which in August is after about 14:30 NZST; 305 deg and 25 deg up is about 15:00, inferred, not read from the photographs. Without this block the sun is the Clock Tower's July morning, low in the north-east and full on this end. A sunlit street below the horizon (ground, groundshade, as Old Government House's) lights the shaded end from below. The camera exposed for the shade, so the white cladding is near white in every photograph: with sky_mask.pale_tint keeping it in the building region, the region's luma median is 237-253 in the photographs (248 on the mean of the nine views). Exposure 2.2 (round 2) brings the drawn median to 241-242, within 11.2 of every view's and 6 on the mean; at 1.3 (round 1) it was 230-233, 16 below on the mean, and at 1.7 237-239, five views more than 12 below. The panes are the kit's glassPale (round 2): the photographs' glass reflects the sunlit buildings across the street (luma 90-130), where the kit's glass drew 15-40.

refine.note: refine corrects no camera from where streetview.camera_fixes puts them (round 2, 2026-10-27). With the cladding solid in the masks (sky_mask.pale_tint) the sky round each silhouette is 5-27% and the solid 53-71%, the white neighbours either side and the tower behind standing next to it, so the reliability test (min_sky 0.2, max_solid 0.5) applies no search; the searches ran to their bounds (dx +2.1 to +3.0 m, dy +0.6 to +1.0 m), pulled toward those neighbours. min_gain is the default again (round 1 set 0.2 while the masks took the cladding for sky).

sky_mask.note: tools/sky_mask.py: the street end's white cladding is in open shade and the camera exposed for it, so it is as white as a hazy sky (R = G = B 233-254, blue minus red -4 to +2 in every box measured) and the masks took it for pale sky wherever it touches the top of a view (35-56% of the model's own pixels in the door views, 48% in mdk1's wide view). With pale_tint 8 the pale sky must be tinted blue (the sky's pale blue here is 18-21 above red): 0-4% of the model's pixels are then sky in every view; the sky's own clipped white over the raked corner in mdk1's wide view goes to solid with the cladding. 4 to 16 give 0-5% too.

door.note: view frame: the foot of the street end's north-west corner on Eden Crescent's footway, 0.5 m in front of its face. The LiDAR ground within a metre of it is 17.54 m (-0.09/-0.06/-0.03 m p10/p50/p90 from ground), so the model's y is 0 there. The street falls south-east along the end, to -0.6 m at the entrance and -1.0 m at the south-east corner: the end's foot (FOOT -1.3) reaches below it everywhere. place.py puts it on the map
